facts.text: Hamilton County eviction cases are filed in Hamilton Superior Court No. 4, 6, or 7, all at One Hamilton County Square in Noblesville (county Local Rule 103.40). Noblesville is the county seat, so the courts are downtown.

facts.label: Property tax
facts.text: A rental isn’t a homestead, so Indiana caps its property tax at 2% of assessed value, against 1% for an owner-occupied home. Hamilton County bills in May and November installments; the 2026 certified rate for the Noblesville City district was 2.5549 per $100 of assessed value.

facts.label: Utilities
facts.text: Water comes from Indiana American Water. Sewer is Noblesville Utilities, the city utility, which also bills city trash service.

facts.label: Location
facts.text: About 24 miles north-northeast of downtown Indianapolis by SR 37 and I-69. Downtown is built around the Hamilton County Courthouse square, completed in 1879 and on the National Register since 1978, and Ruoff Music Center is in the city.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Noblesville?
faqs.a: No. As of September 2026, Noblesville’s city code has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement and no rental cap. Rentals are held to the same housing and property maintenance code as any other home, and HOA covenants can add their own rules.

faqs.q: Where are evictions filed for a Noblesville rental?
faqs.a: In Hamilton Superior Court No. 4, 6, or 7, at One Hamilton County Square in Noblesville. Under the county’s Local Rule 103.40, all Hamilton County eviction and small claims cases go to those three courts, wherever in the county the rental is.

facts.label: Rental registration
facts.text: None for long-term rentals. Westfield’s code of ordinances has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement and no rental cap.

facts.label: Eviction filings
facts.text: Hamilton County eviction cases are filed in Hamilton Superior Court No. 4, 6, or 7, all at One Hamilton County Square in Noblesville (county Local Rule 103.40).

facts.label: Property tax
facts.text: A rental isn’t a homestead, so Indiana caps its property tax at 2% of assessed value, against 1% for an owner-occupied home. Hamilton County bills in May and November installments; the 2026 certified rate for the Westfield district was 2.3448 per $100 of assessed value.

facts.label: Utilities
facts.text: Water and sewer come from Citizens Westfield, part of Citizens Energy Group, which bought the city’s systems in 2014. Gas is Citizens Westfield in part of the city and CenterPoint Energy (formerly Vectren) in the rest.

facts.label: Location
facts.text: About 20 miles north of downtown Indianapolis by US 31 (Meridian Street). Grand Park Sports Campus, more than 400 acres with 26 diamonds, is in Westfield, and the Monon Trail runs through the city.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Westfield?
faqs.a: Not for a long-term rental. Westfield’s city code has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement and no rental cap. HOA covenants can add their own rules, so check them before renting.

faqs.q: Where are evictions filed for a Westfield rental?
faqs.a: In Hamilton Superior Court No. 4, 6, or 7, at One Hamilton County Square in Noblesville. Under the county’s Local Rule 103.40, all Hamilton County eviction and small claims cases go to those three courts, wherever in the county the rental is.

facts.label: Rental registration
facts.text: None. Avon’s municipal code and development ordinance have no registration, licensing, or inspection requirement for long-term rentals. The one rental-specific rule (Code 7-87): in a rented home, the owner or manager must install the required smoke detectors and repair or replace one within two business days of written notice.

facts.label: Short-term rentals
facts.text: A town permit is required before a home is used as a short-term rental (UDO 4.11). The owner must post a 24/7 contact who has a key and can be on site within three hours, along with the maximum occupancy and parking instructions.

facts.label: Eviction filings
facts.text: Hendricks County eviction cases are filed in Hendricks Superior Court No. 1, 3, 4, or 5, assigned at random, at the courthouse in Danville.

facts.label: Property tax
facts.text: A rental isn’t a homestead, so Indiana caps its property tax at 2% of assessed value, against 1% for an owner-occupied home (voter-approved referendum levies sit outside the cap). The Hendricks County Treasurer bills in May and November installments.

facts.label: Utilities
facts.text: Per the town, water is Citizens Energy Group, sewer is the West Central Conservancy District, and gas is CenterPoint Energy. Electric depends on location: Duke Energy, Hendricks Power Cooperative, or AES Indiana. Avon has no town trash service; owners or tenants hire a private hauler.

facts.label: Location
facts.text: About 13 miles west of downtown Indianapolis on US 36, the main east-west road through town, with the Ronald Reagan Parkway running north-south through it. The White Lick Creek Trail runs along the creek through Washington Township Park.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Avon?
faqs.a: No. Avon has no registration, licensing, or inspection requirement for long-term rentals. The town does require owners of rented homes to install smoke detectors and fix one within two business days of written notice, and a short-term rental needs a town permit.

faqs.q: Where are evictions filed for a Avon rental?
faqs.a: In Hendricks Superior Court No. 1, 3, 4, or 5 at the Hendricks County Courthouse, 51 W. Main St., Danville. Under the county’s local rules, eviction cases are assigned among those four courts at random.

facts.label: Rental registration
facts.text: None. Brownsburg’s code of ordinances (current through August 2026) has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement.

facts.label: Eviction filings
facts.text: Hendricks County eviction cases are filed in Hendricks Superior Court No. 1, 3, 4, or 5, assigned at random, at the courthouse in Danville.

facts.label: Property tax
facts.text: A rental isn’t a homestead, so Indiana caps its property tax at 2% of assessed value, against 1% for an owner-occupied home (voter-approved referendum levies sit outside the cap). The Hendricks County Treasurer bills in May and November installments.

facts.label: Utilities
facts.text: The town runs water and sewer on one monthly bill. A tenant opening an account provides a copy of the lease and pays a $100 sewer deposit on top of the $75 water meter deposit.

facts.label: Location
facts.text: About 13 miles west-northwest of downtown Indianapolis, with I-74 exits at Green Street (SR 267) and the Ronald Reagan Parkway, and US 136 running through town. The 8.2-mile B&O Trail, the White Lick Creek Greenway to Arbuckle Acres Park, and the Bicentennial Trail link to Avon, which borders Brownsburg to the south.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Brownsburg?
faqs.a: No. As of August 2026, Brownsburg’s town code has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement. When a tenant opens the water and sewer account, the town asks for a copy of the lease and a $100 sewer deposit in addition to the $75 water meter deposit.

faqs.q: Where are evictions filed for a Brownsburg rental?
faqs.a: In Hendricks Superior Court No. 1, 3, 4, or 5 at the Hendricks County Courthouse, 51 W. Main St., Danville. Under the county’s local rules, eviction cases are assigned among those four courts at random.

facts.label: Rental registration
facts.text: None. Zionsville’s code of ordinances has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement.

facts.label: Eviction filings
facts.text: Boone County eviction cases are filed in Boone Superior Court II, which hears all of the county’s small claims, at the Boone County Courthouse, 112 Courthouse Square, Lebanon.

facts.label: Property tax
facts.text: A rental isn’t a homestead, so Indiana caps its property tax at 2% of assessed value, against 1% for an owner-occupied home (voter-approved referendum levies sit outside the cap). The Boone County Treasurer bills in May and November installments.

facts.label: Utilities
facts.text: Water is Citizens Water. Sewer is the town’s own utility, billed at a flat residential rate ($56.85 a month as of January 2025), with trash and recycling in the town’s urban service district on the same bill.

facts.label: Location
facts.text: About 15 miles northwest of downtown Indianapolis, served by I-65 and I-865, with US 421 (Michigan Road) along its east side. The paved Big-4 Rail Trail is the five-mile spine of more than 20 miles of connected paths, and the historic brick Main Street village is the town center.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Zionsville?
faqs.a: No. Zionsville’s town code has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement. HOA covenants can add their own rules, so check them before renting.

faqs.q: Where are evictions filed for a Zionsville rental?
faqs.a: In Boone Superior Court II at the Boone County Courthouse, 112 Courthouse Square, Lebanon. That court has exclusive jurisdiction over all Boone County small claims cases, including evictions.

facts.label: Rental registration
facts.text: None. Greenwood’s code of ordinances (current through July 2026) has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement.

facts.label: Eviction filings
facts.text: Johnson County eviction cases are filed in the Johnson Circuit and Superior Courts, assigned at random and heard by the courts’ magistrate, at the courthouse in Franklin. Greenwood City Court does not hear evictions.

facts.label: Property tax
facts.text: A rental isn’t a homestead, so Indiana caps its property tax at 2% of assessed value, against 1% for an owner-occupied home (voter-approved referendum levies sit outside the cap). The Johnson County Treasurer bills in May and November installments.

facts.label: Utilities
facts.text: City sewer bills go to the property owner every month, not the tenant, and service is started or stopped through the water provider. Water is Indiana American Water or Bargersville Water depending on the address, and city trash is added to the sewer account.

facts.label: Location
facts.text: About 11 miles south of downtown Indianapolis, with three I-65 exits on the east side, I-69 just west of city limits, and US 31 and SR 135 as the main north-south streets. The city lists more than 50 miles of multi-use trails and runs the Freedom Springs aquatic center and Greenwood Sports Park.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Greenwood?
faqs.a: No. As of July 2026, Greenwood’s city code has no rental registration, licensing, or inspection requirement. City sewer is billed to the property owner monthly, not the tenant, so it belongs in an owner’s operating budget.

faqs.q: Where are evictions filed for a Greenwood rental?
faqs.a: In the Johnson Circuit and Superior Courts at the Johnson County Courthouse in Franklin, where small claims cases, including evictions, are assigned at random and heard by the magistrate. Greenwood City Court does not handle evictions.
